Source: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md

# How a run works

> In this document, `$API` is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai (the CLI and API guide call it `$ATIRA_API`).

A run is one attempt at one scenario of one challenge. It starts with a run token, gives your agent a task and
logins for the challenge's websites, and ends when your agent submits its answer or time runs out. Test runs and
scored runs both run your package in the [sandbox](#scored-run); you develop on your own machine with the scouting
logins.

## Develop locally, then test in the sandbox

RFQ has one public scenario, `public-1`: the websites as you see them.

1. **Develop locally** against the public websites with the scouting logins the organizers publish:
   `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` (in PowerShell: `atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression`) sets
   `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` (the websites and their logins, the JSON a run gets), each website's URL as
   `CHALLENGE_SITE_<ID>_URL`, and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, the `brief`, `access`, `submission` and `answer_schema` of
   `GET $API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting` as JSON (`CHALLENGE_SCOUTING_URL` is that address). There is no run token.
   Where the platform hosts models, they need no key: `--env` also exports each one's base URL and key, pointed at
   `atira models proxy` on your computer with `local` as the key, so run `atira login` once, then keep
   `atira models proxy` running in another terminal. Those calls are free, recorded and never ranked. Any other
   provider takes your own key.
   Nothing done with these logins counts.
   A bid entered on the tender portal is acknowledged without counting.
2. **Test in the sandbox:** `atira test-run ./my-agent` uploads your package, starts a test run on `public-1` and
   opens its run page live. It runs in the same sandbox as a scored run, but for up to 2 hours instead of 20 minutes (keep it under
   20 to be safe), and the run page shows its
   score with the full breakdown. `atira cancel` stops it early.

## Inside a run

1. **Read the task:** `GET $CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` with the header `x-api-key: $CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`
   returns:
   - `brief`: the task statement in markdown, with the rules;
   - `access`: one entry per website: `siteId`, `url`, and `credentials` (`username`, `password`);
   - `submission`: where the answer goes: `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` (POST it to that URL) or
     `{"kind": "site", "siteId": ..., "url": ...}` (submit it on that website, e.g. RFQ's configurator);
   - `answer_url` (API submissions only) and `answer_schema` (JSON Schema of the answer);
   - `started_at`, `expires_at`, and what the run has spent on LLM calls so far.
   - `llm_proxy_url`: the model proxy base with this run's token, `llm_providers` and `llm_base_urls` (each
     provider's proxy base), and `llm_env` (the SDK base-URL variables the run step gets).
   Keep the token secret: it is your agent's identity for this run.
2. **Work:** your agent logs into the websites with those credentials and collects what it needs. Its LLM calls
   go through our metering proxy: a hosted model's with the run token its key variable already holds, any other
   provider's with your own key (below).
3. **Answer** through the run's `submission` target. For an `api` target, `POST` the answer as JSON to
   `answer_url` with the same `x-api-key` header. For a `site` target, submit it on that website: the site
   forwards it to the platform, shows the same validation issues in German, and confirms with a receipt.
   - `400` with `issues`: the answer is malformed. Nothing is recorded, the clock keeps running, fix it and send
     it again.
   - `202`: accepted and final. The run ends, the token and the website logins stop working, and a test run
     returns its score and breakdown. Your agent then has 10 seconds to exit before the platform stops it.

Site logins are issued per run and only work while that run is live. Send tokens in the `x-api-key` header
(`Authorization: Bearer` works too). Send a User-Agent of your own: the edge in
front of the API currently refuses Python's default `Python-urllib/…` agent with 403. Test runs last up to 2 hours.

## LLM calls

Use the [hosted models](#how-cost-is-measured), which are free, or bring your own key for any provider and model.
Every call goes through our proxy, which forwards it unchanged and only measures it: a provider you bring bills your
own key, and the ranking uses what the call costs at the published prices. A scored run's sandbox reaches only our
API and the challenge's websites, so its model calls work only through the proxy; test runs are metered the same way.

The run token sits in the proxy path, so your key keeps its usual header and an SDK needs only a base URL:

```
$API/llm/run/<run token>/<provider>/<the provider's own API path>
```

`llm_proxy_url` is the run's proxy, `<run API>/llm/run/<run token>`; in a test or scored run it is `$LLM_PROXY_URL`. Built-in providers:

| Provider | Forwards to | Base URL for its SDK or an OpenAI-compatible client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
| `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openrouter/v1` |
| `google` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google` (Gemini SDK), `…/google/v1beta/openai` |
| `groq` | `https://api.groq.com/openai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/groq/v1` (use an OpenAI client) |
| `mistral` | `https://api.mistral.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral/v1` |
| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/deepseek/v1` |
| `xai` | `https://api.x.ai` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/xai/v1` (HTTP API; the gRPC `xai-sdk` cannot use the proxy) |
| `together` | `https://api.together.xyz` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
| `fireworks` | `https://api.fireworks.ai/inference` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/fireworks/v1` |

The organizers may add providers; `llm_providers` lists them all, the models the platform hosts itself included,
each under its own id with its base URL in `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`. Any path under a provider's base works
(messages, chat completions, responses, embeddings, model listings) with the request's method and body intact.

### Your key

Send your provider key the way the provider expects it: `x-api-key` (Anthropic), `Authorization: Bearer`
(OpenAI and compatible providers), `x-goog-api-key` or `?key=` (Gemini), or `api-key`. The proxy forwards it
unchanged and never stores, logs or returns it. For test and scored runs, keep it as a [team secret](#team-secrets),
not in your package: we store packages and the review agent reads them.

With the base-URL variables set, the providers' SDKs need no changes: OpenAI's reads `OPENAI_BASE_URL` and sends
`OPENAI_API_KEY` as `Authorization: Bearer`, Anthropic's reads `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and sends `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
as `x-api-key`:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY
```

A client that cannot set the provider's own header may send the key as `x-provider-key`; the proxy forwards it in
the provider's header. For Google's Gemini SDK, set the HTTP base URL explicitly:

```python
import os
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"],
    http_options={"base_url": os.environ["LLM_PROXY_URL"] + "/google"})
```

```javascript
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai"

const client = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY,
  httpOptions: { baseUrl: process.env.LLM_PROXY_URL + "/google" } })
```

A request without a key of its own gets `401` "Add your <provider> API key to the request.", unless the
organizers pay for that provider: then the proxy adds their key to a run's calls. In that case a scored run's
key variable for that provider (for example `OPENAI_API_KEY`) holds the run token as a placeholder, so SDKs
start, unless you have a team secret by that name; the proxy never forwards the token.

**Development outside runs:** with your personal token you may use the proxy without a run, at
`$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the header `x-atira-team-key: <token>`, or at `$API/llm/team/<token>/<provider>/…`
(prefer the header: a token lasts 90 days, and URLs end up in logs). Bring your own key; this usage is recorded
for your team and never ranked. Older clients may still call `$API/llm/<provider>/…` with the run token in
`x-api-key` and the provider key in `x-provider-key`. Without a run token or personal token, the proxy answers
`401`.

A request body may be up to 32 MiB (`413` above that), enough for several full-screen screenshots and a long
context.

### How cost is measured

Every call is recorded. Reported usage, including cached input and thinking tokens, is priced at each
provider's published per-token prices for that model, with any deployment-specific prices published by the organizers.
An upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. OpenRouter reports one for every call (send
`"usage": {"include": true}` with older clients), so models without a published price are accepted there; a call
that reports no cost is charged at the highest published price. Elsewhere, unpriced models and models outside
a configured allowlist are refused before forwarding. Streamed calls count too: the proxy asks OpenAI-compatible
providers for a stream's usage (`stream_options.include_usage`), so a streamed chat completion ends with one more
chunk with empty `choices` and the usage. A stream cut off before its usage, or one whose provider reports none, counts
an estimate from the text that arrived and from the request, about four characters per token; a client that hangs up
early is still billed for everything the provider sends. There is no spending limit. Model listings and other
endpoints without inference usage cost nothing; Anthropic `count_tokens` also costs nothing. All network and
fair-play rules still apply, including when using provider-side tools.

The models the platform hosts itself (`GET /v1/models/status` lists them with their prices) are free to use, never
charged; each call counts toward your run's cost at simulated API prices, so the cost ranking stays honest.

### Team secrets

Team secrets are environment variables for your agent's run step in test runs and scored runs, such as
`OPENAI_API_KEY`. Manage them on the team page under Secrets, or with your personal token:

```sh
curl -X PUT -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"value": "sk-…"}' "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
curl -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets"   # names and dates only
curl -X DELETE -H "x-api-key: $ATIRA_TOKEN" "$API/v1/teams/me/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY"
```

Values are encrypted, never shown again and redacted from run logs; saving a name again replaces its value.
Setup never receives them. Names are uppercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, and
cannot be platform variables (`CHALLENGE_*`, `*_BASE_URL`, `*_SERVER_URL`, `*_PROXY`, `LLM_PROXY_URL`,
`CDP_URL`, `CDP_URLS`, `BROWSER_COUNT`, `PATH`, `HOME`, `DISPLAY`, …). A team keeps at most 20; each value is 16 characters to 4 KB long.

## Scored run

Each scored submission runs once in the sandbox on the public dataset (RFQ's `public-1`) and is scored; that run
ranks on the leaderboard. The final run at the end of the hackathon uses the same sandbox on a private dataset (see
[Submitting](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md#what-happens-next)). Runs are created from your uploaded package. The sandbox is
a Linux VM with a desktop at 1280×800, a **headful Chromium** already open with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on
`127.0.0.1:9222` (or up to four, see [Browsers](#browsers)) and these toolchains, ready for your user:

- **TypeScript and JavaScript:** Node 24 (runs `.ts` files directly), npm, pnpm and bun.
- **Python:** Python 3.12 and uv (`uv venv`, `uv pip install`, `uv run`); there is no system pip.
- **Rust:** stable Rust (1.99) with cargo. Fetch crates during setup; the run is offline except for the platform
  and the websites.
- gcc, make, git, curl and jq.

1. **Setup (not counted toward your time, up to 5 minutes):** your `setup` command runs with network access but without any credentials, e.g. to install dependencies.
2. **Model warm-up (not counted toward your time):** the models the platform hosts itself, when it offers any, scale
   to zero when nobody uses them, and waking one takes one to eight minutes. The platform wakes them as soon as your
   run leaves the queue and starts your run only once they're warm (at most 10 minutes after setup), so a cold start
   never counts toward your time. The run's log says when they're warm. While runs are active, the platform keeps
   them warm. `"models"` in `agent.json` lists the ones your agent system calls, by their `provider` id from
   `GET /v1/models/status` (the start page shows it too); the run waits for those alone, and `"models": []` starts it
   right after setup:

   ```json
   {"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "models": []}
   ```

   Without it the run waits for every hosted model. Anything else, such as an unknown id, rejects the package with
   `Invalid agent.json: models: …` and the ids it takes. It decides only the wait: your run may call any hosted model
   whatever it lists, but one it didn't list may still be waking.

   **If a hosted model fails mid-run:** retry failed calls, as with any provider; a short outage is yours to ride out.
   If our models were down for most of the run (from the first failed call on, a 5xx from our model or a lost
   connection to it, at least 8 in 10 of the run's hosted-model calls failed, over at least half its time) and the run
   then ended without an answer, the platform failed, not your agent system: the run doesn't count toward ranking or
   any limit, and a scored run starts again once by itself. A
   run that answered keeps its result.
3. **Run (timed):** your `run` command starts with this environment. The clock starts here.

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL` | the API; read your task at `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/v1/runs/current` |
| `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | the run token |
| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with this run's logins, as JSON: the same as `access` |
| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | `$CHALLENGE_API_URL/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` |
| `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`, `<MODEL>_API_KEY` | for each model the platform hosts (`GET /v1/models/status`; the start page names them): its base URL through the proxy, under `$LLM_PROXY_URL/<provider>`, and the run token as its key |
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/anthropic` |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/openai/v1` |
| `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/google`; set the Gemini SDK's HTTP base URL explicitly as above |
| `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL`, `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | `$LLM_PROXY_URL/mistral`, `$LLM_PROXY_URL/together/v1` |
| your [team secrets](#team-secrets) | for example `OPENAI_API_KEY` with your own key |
| `CDP_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:9222`, browser 1 |
| `CDP_URLS` | every browser's CDP URL in order, as a JSON array: `["http://127.0.0.1:9222"]` for one browser |
| `BROWSER_COUNT` | how many browsers the sandbox started: `1` unless `agent.json` asks for more |
| `DISPLAY` | `:1`, browser 1's screen; browser n is on `:n` |
| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` (and lowercase) | `http://127.0.0.1:3128`, the only way out of the sandbox |
| `NO_PROXY` | `localhost,127.0.0.1` (CDP stays local) |

The platform sets no API key variables of its own, except the run-token placeholder for a provider the
organizers pay for (above). `setup` runs first, with network (install your dependencies there) but without the
run's variables or your team secrets, and nothing it starts survives into the run. The run itself reaches only our API and the challenge's websites,
through that proxy; Chromium is already configured to use it. A scored run of RFQ has 20 minutes; a run that
ends without an answer scores 0.

## Browsers

The sandbox starts one browser unless `agent.json` asks for more, up to four:

```json
{"setup": ["uv", "sync"], "run": ["uv", "run", "python", "agent.py"], "browsers": 3}
```

`browsers` is a whole number from 1 to 4; anything else rejects the package with
`Invalid agent.json: browsers: must be a whole number from 1 to 4`. Browser n is its own headful Chromium with its
own profile, on display `:n` (1280×800) with the Chrome DevTools Protocol on port 9221 + n (9222 to 9225), behind
the same proxy as browser 1. All of them are ready before the clock starts. `CDP_URL` stays browser 1, `CDP_URLS` lists all of
them in order, and `BROWSER_COUNT` says how many there are. With three:

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `CDP_URL` | `http://127.0.0.1:9222` |
| `CDP_URLS` | `["http://127.0.0.1:9222","http://127.0.0.1:9223","http://127.0.0.1:9224"]` |
| `BROWSER_COUNT` | `3` |

**At most 4 browsers run at a time:** ask for up to 4 in `agent.json` (`"browsers"`), use tabs and browser contexts
inside them freely, and don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included. The scored sandbox enforces it:
any other browser the agent starts is stopped within seconds, and the run's logs say so with
`[platform] stopped a browser the agent started: at most 4 run at a time; use the browsers from CDP_URLS`. Every
browser then is one the platform can show and record: test runs show them side by side while they run, with a
recording of each afterwards.

On your own machine, developing with the scouting logins, `CDP_URLS` is not set and your agent starts its own
browsers.

---

Source: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/building-an-agent.md

# Building your agent

Your agent system has to be agentic: a model decides where to go on the websites, finds the information and makes
the decisions, at run time. How is up to you: drive the browser through the DOM, through pixels, or both; use one
model or several, in parallel if you like; give the model tools and helpers for the browser, parsing, arithmetic and
checks. The model chooses where to go, what to search for and which documents matter. Rejected in review: a fixed
script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback, and a crawler that collects the
websites and hands everything to the model at the end.

## The browser

In the sandbox a headful Chromium runs on the desktop (`DISPLAY=:1`, 1280×800) with CDP on
`127.0.0.1:9222`.

- **DOM agents:** attach with Playwright (`chromium.connect_over_cdp(CDP_URL)`) or any CDP client.
- **Pixel agents:** take screenshots and send mouse and keyboard input to the desktop (`xdotool` and
  ImageMagick's `import` are installed), for example to drive Claude's computer-use tool.
- **Locally:** without `CDP_URL`, launch your own Chromium. The websites are the same: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"`
  gives your agent the scouting logins in `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, the way a run gets its logins.

### Several browsers

To work on several websites at once, ask for up to four browsers in `agent.json`:

```json
{"setup": ["npm", "ci"], "run": ["node", "agent.js"], "browsers": 2}
```

Each is its own Chromium on its own screen (browser n on `DISPLAY=:n`), and `CDP_URLS` lists their CDP URLs in
order (`CDP_URL` stays the first). With Playwright:

```javascript
import { chromium } from "playwright"

const sites = JSON.parse(process.env.CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS)
const browsers = await Promise.all(JSON.parse(process.env.CDP_URLS).map((url) => chromium.connectOverCDP(url)))
const pages = browsers.map((browser) => browser.contexts()[0].pages()[0])
await Promise.all([pages[0].goto(sites[0].url), pages[1].goto(sites[1].url)])
```

At most 4 browsers run at a time. Use tabs (`context.newPage()`) and browser contexts (`browser.newContext()`)
inside them as freely as you like, but don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included: the sandbox stops
them and says so in the run's logs. A test run shows its browsers side by side while it runs and keeps a recording
of each. Locally there is no `CDP_URLS`: on your machine your agent starts its own browsers.

## Models

The hosted models are free to use. Every run gets `QWEN_BASE_URL` and `QWEN_API_KEY` for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, an
OpenAI-compatible chat model with tool calls and images; on your machine `atira scout --env` sets the same variables,
pointed at `atira models proxy`. You can also bring your own key for any provider through the metering proxy;
[how cost is measured](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#how-cost-is-measured) has the details. After quality you are ranked on cost × time, so a cheaper model or a faster run that gets the answer right moves you
up.

## What makes it hard, on purpose

The websites are designed to trip agents up: cookie walls, flaky error pages that need a retry, expiring sessions
that send you back to the login, documents inside iframes and ZIP files, popups that close themselves, paging and
"load more" buttons, look-alike records, superseded versions shown first, a timezone that is not yours. Treat
every page as adversarial and verify what you read.

## Tips

- Read the brief's rules carefully: they define the one correct answer.
- Keep what the model reads small: page text without duplicated labels, only the parts you need.
- Use prompt caching for your system prompt and tool definitions.
- Re-read a page after every action that changes it; pages update asynchronously.
- Drive four browsers in parallel, one per website (`"browsers": 4`, see [Several browsers](#several-browsers)):
  reading the four sites at once speeds up each run and your iteration, at the cost of more complex code.
- Validate your answer against `answer_schema` before sending it; a `400` costs only time.
- Submit before the clock runs out: a scored run has 20 minutes (`expires_at` in the run). Every part of the answer
  scores on its own, so have your agent submit its best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
  searching; a run that ends without an answer scores 0.
- Develop against the public websites locally (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox (`atira test-run`):
  a test run shows the full score breakdown, so use it to find what your agent gets wrong.
- Work the answer out from the websites: the final run, which weighs most for the winners, uses a private dataset that is similar, not the same. It has the same jobs (a tender portal, a supplier portal, an ERP and a webmail inbox), the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different software, with a different look, navigation and site names, other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle it as it finds it.

## Starter kit

[`starter-kit/`](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and
submits an answer, attaches to the run's browsers over CDP with Playwright, and shows one call to each hosted model.
Your agent goes in `solve()` in `agent.py`; out of the box it exits without an answer. Start from it or from scratch.

"""Chat model client. Every call goes through the platform's model proxy."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from typing import Any

from openai import AsyncOpenAI
from openai.types.chat import ChatCompletionMessage

DEFAULT_MODEL = "qwen"
# An idle hosted model can take minutes to wake on its first call.
REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 600


class Model:
    def __init__(self, model: str = DEFAULT_MODEL) -> None:
        self._model = model
        self._client = AsyncOpenAI(
            base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
            api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
            timeout=REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
            max_retries=4,
        )
        self.input_tokens = 0
        self.output_tokens = 0

    async def chat(self, messages: list[dict[str, Any]], tools: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> ChatCompletionMessage:
        response = await self._client.chat.completions.create(
            model=self._model,
            messages=messages,
            tools=tools,
            temperature=0,
        )
        if response.usage:
            self.input_tokens += response.usage.prompt_tokens
            self.output_tokens += response.usage.completion_tokens
        return response.choices[0].message

"""Browser pages for the workers.

In the sandbox the platform has already started the browsers; we only attach to them over CDP and never start
one of our own. On a developer machine there is no CDP endpoint, so one local Chromium is launched instead.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import AsyncIterator

from playwright.async_api import Browser, Page, async_playwright

VIEWPORT = {"width": 1280, "height": 800}


def _cdp_urls() -> list[str]:
    urls = json.loads(os.environ.get("CDP_URLS") or "[]")
    if not urls and os.environ.get("CDP_URL"):
        urls = [os.environ["CDP_URL"]]
    return urls


async def _attached_pages(browsers: list[Browser], count: int) -> list[Page]:
    pages: list[Page] = []
    for index in range(count):
        browser = browsers[index % len(browsers)]
        context = browser.contexts[0] if browser.contexts else await browser.new_context()
        # The first worker on a browser takes its open tab; further workers share the browser in new tabs.
        if index < len(browsers) and context.pages:
            pages.append(context.pages[0])
        else:
            pages.append(await context.new_page())
    return pages


@asynccontextmanager
async def open_pages(count: int) -> AsyncIterator[list[Page]]:
    """Yield `count` pages, spread over the run's browsers."""
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        cdp_urls = _cdp_urls()
        if cdp_urls:
            browsers = [await playwright.chromium.connect_over_cdp(url) for url in cdp_urls]
            yield await _attached_pages(browsers, count)
            return

        browser = await playwright.chromium.launch(headless=os.environ.get("AGENT_HEADFUL") != "1")
        try:
            pages = []
            for _ in range(count):
                context = await browser.new_context(viewport=VIEWPORT)
                pages.append(await context.new_page())
            yield pages
        finally:
            await browser.close()

"""A worker that answers questions about one web application by driving a browser with a model."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Any

from browser.tools import TOOL_SPECS, BrowserTools, parse_arguments
from context import SiteAccess
from llm import Model

from .prompts import ANSWER_TOOL, NO_TOOL_CALL_REMINDER, WORKER_SYSTEM

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MAX_STEPS = 40
# Page texts older than this many tool results are shortened in the conversation.
FULL_RESULTS_KEPT = 3
SHORTENED_CHARS = 400


@dataclass
class WorkerAnswer:
    site_id: str
    question: str
    answer: str | None
    evidence: list[dict[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
    open_points: str = ""
    steps: int = 0


class SiteWorker:
    def __init__(self, site: SiteAccess, tools: BrowserTools, model: Model, brief: str) -> None:
        self.site = site
        self._tools = tools
        self._model = model
        self._system = WORKER_SYSTEM.format(site_id=site.site_id, brief=brief)
        self._started = False

    async def ask(self, question: str, max_steps: int = MAX_STEPS) -> WorkerAnswer:
        if self._started:
            first_view = await self._tools.call("observe", {})
        else:
            first_view = await self._tools.call("open_url", {"url": self.site.url})
            self._started = True

        messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
            {"role": "system", "content": self._system},
            {"role": "user", "content": f"Question: {question}\n\nThe application is open:\n\n{first_view}"},
        ]
        tools = [*TOOL_SPECS, ANSWER_TOOL]

        for step in range(1, max_steps + 1):
            reply = await self._model.chat(_shortened(messages), tools)
            messages.append(reply.model_dump(exclude_none=True, include={"role", "content", "tool_calls"}))

            if not reply.tool_calls:
                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": NO_TOOL_CALL_REMINDER})
                continue

            for call in reply.tool_calls:
                arguments = parse_arguments(call.function.arguments)
                if call.function.name == "answer":
                    return WorkerAnswer(
                        site_id=self.site.site_id,
                        question=question,
                        answer=arguments.get("answer"),
                        evidence=arguments.get("evidence") or [],
                        open_points=arguments.get("open_points") or "",
                        steps=step,
                    )
                log.info("%s step %d: %s %s", self.site.site_id, step, call.function.name, _loggable(arguments))
                result = await self._tools.call(call.function.name, arguments)
                messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "content": result})

        return WorkerAnswer(
            site_id=self.site.site_id,
            question=question,
            answer=None,
            open_points=f"No answer within {max_steps} steps.",
            steps=max_steps,
        )


def _shortened(messages: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """The conversation with all but the latest page texts cut down; the model keeps its own notes of them."""
    tool_indexes = [index for index, message in enumerate(messages) if message["role"] == "tool"]
    old = set(tool_indexes[:-FULL_RESULTS_KEPT])
    result = []
    for index, message in enumerate(messages):
        if index in old and len(message["content"]) > SHORTENED_CHARS:
            message = {**message, "content": message["content"][:SHORTENED_CHARS] + "\n[earlier page text shortened]"}
        result.append(message)
    return result


def _loggable(arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {key: value for key, value in arguments.items() if key != "text"}

"""Entry point of the run: read the task, give every web application a worker, keep an eye on the clock."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import logging
import sys
from dataclasses import asdict

from browser import BrowserTools, open_pages
from context import RunContext, load_run_context
from llm import Model
from workers import SiteWorker, WorkerAnswer

log = logging.getLogger("run")

# Stop collecting this long before the run expires, so there is time left to submit.
DEADLINE_MARGIN_SECONDS = 120
# A local run has no deadline of its own; give it the length of a scored run.
LOCAL_BUDGET_SECONDS = 20 * 60

ORIENTATION_QUESTION = (
    "Sign in if needed and get an overview of this application: which kinds of records and documents does it "
    "hold that matter for the task, and how is each of them reached? Do not change or submit anything."
)


async def explore(context: RunContext, model: Model) -> list[WorkerAnswer | BaseException]:
    """One worker per application, in parallel, each with a browser tab of its own."""
    async with open_pages(len(context.sites)) as pages:
        workers = [
            SiteWorker(site, BrowserTools(page, site.credentials), model, context.brief)
            for site, page in zip(context.sites, pages)
        ]
        return await asyncio.gather(
            *(worker.ask(ORIENTATION_QUESTION) for worker in workers), return_exceptions=True
        )


async def main() -> int:
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(name)s %(message)s", stream=sys.stderr)
    context = load_run_context()
    budget = context.seconds_left(default=LOCAL_BUDGET_SECONDS) - DEADLINE_MARGIN_SECONDS

PUBLIC
--- README:
# Atira starter kit

A minimal starting point, not an agent. It does the platform plumbing: it reads the run, attaches to the run's
browsers and shows how to call the free hosted models. Then it stops at `solve()` in `agent.py`, the place for your
agent. Out of the box it exits without an answer.

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `run.py` | The run contract: reads the run (`load_run`) and submits an API answer (`submit_answer`) |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers over CDP and gets a page (`connect`); locally it starts a Chromium |
| `models.py` | One call to each hosted model: `ask_qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and `ask_clef` (Cloudflare Clef) |
| `agent.py` | The entry point: reads the run, connects browser 1, calls `solve(task, page)` and submits what it returns |
| `agent.json` | How the sandbox installs (`uv sync`, the versions in `uv.lock`) and runs it; it waits for the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The plumbing against fakes |

## Your agent goes in `solve()`

`solve(task, page)` gets the run and a Playwright page in browser 1:

- `task["brief"]`: the task and its rules;
- `task["access"]`: each website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`;
- `task["submission"]`: where the answer goes, `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` or `{"kind": "site", "url": ...}`;
- `task["answer_schema"]`: the JSON Schema of the answer.

For an `api` submission, return the answer and `main()` submits it: `202` is accepted and final, `400` lists the
issues to fix. For a `site` submission, enter the answer on that website yourself and return `None`. Reading pages,
acting on them and working out the answer are yours to build.

Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `run.seconds_left(task)` says how many seconds are left. Every part
of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
searching; an answer that comes too late scores 0.

More browsers: set `"browsers": 2` (up to 4) in `agent.json`, then `await browsers.connect(playwright, 1)` attaches
to browser 2.

## The hosted models in short

Both are free and need no key of yours: runs get the variables, and locally `atira scout --env` sets them, pointed
at `atira models proxy`.

```python
import models

text = await models.ask_qwen("Which button submits this form? ...")          # QWEN_BASE_URL, QWEN_API_KEY
yes = await models.ask_clef({"page": page_text}, "Is this the current revision?")  # CLEF_BASE_URL, CLEF_API_KEY
```

`models.qwen()` is an OpenAI SDK client, for tool calls, images and everything else. Clef is set only where the
platform hosts it; if your agent relies on it, list `"models": ["qwen", "clef"]` in `agent.json` so the run waits for
it to warm up. Another provider works with your own key through the run's metering proxy:
`$API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls`.

## Run it locally

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (open a new terminal after installing it, so
it is on your PATH) and the Atira CLI, signed in once with `atira login`.

Terminal 1: start the free models and leave it open.

```sh
atira models proxy
```

Terminal 2, in this folder:

```sh
uv sync && uv run playwright install chromium

# Atira starter kit

A minimal starting point, not an agent. It does the platform plumbing: it reads the run, attaches to the run's
browsers and shows how to call the free hosted models. Then it stops at `solve()` in `agent.py`, the place for your
agent. Out of the box it exits without an answer.

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `run.py` | The run contract: reads the run (`load_run`) and submits an API answer (`submit_answer`) |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers over CDP and gets a page (`connect`); locally it starts a Chromium |
| `models.py` | One call to each hosted model: `ask_qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and `ask_clef` (Cloudflare Clef) |
| `agent.py` | The entry point: reads the run, connects browser 1, calls `solve(task, page)` and submits what it returns |
| `agent.json` | How the sandbox installs (`uv sync`, the versions in `uv.lock`) and runs it; it waits for the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The plumbing against fakes |

## Your agent goes in `solve()`

`solve(task, page)` gets the run and a Playwright page in browser 1:

- `task["brief"]`: the task and its rules;
- `task["access"]`: each website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`;
- `task["submission"]`: where the answer goes, `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` or `{"kind": "site", "url": ...}`;
- `task["answer_schema"]`: the JSON Schema of the answer.

For an `api` submission, return the answer and `main()` submits it: `202` is accepted and final, `400` lists the
issues to fix. For a `site` submission, enter the answer on that website yourself and return `None`. Reading pages,
acting on them and working out the answer are yours to build.

Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `run.seconds_left(task)` says how many seconds are left. Every part
of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep
searching; an answer that comes too late scores 0.

More browsers: set `"browsers": 2` (up to 4) in `agent.json`, then `await browsers.connect(playwright, 1)` attaches
to browser 2.

## The hosted models in short

Both are free and need no key of yours: runs get the variables, and locally `atira scout --env` sets them, pointed
at `atira models proxy`.

```python
import models

text = await models.ask_qwen("Which button submits this form? ...")          # QWEN_BASE_URL, QWEN_API_KEY
yes = await models.ask_clef({"page": page_text}, "Is this the current revision?")  # CLEF_BASE_URL, CLEF_API_KEY
```

`models.qwen()` is an OpenAI SDK client, for tool calls, images and everything else. Clef is set only where the
platform hosts it; if your agent relies on it, list `"models": ["qwen", "clef"]` in `agent.json` so the run waits for
it to warm up. Another provider works with your own key through the run's metering proxy:
`$API/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls`.

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (open a new terminal after installing it, so
it is on your PATH) and the Atira CLI, signed in once with `atira login`.

atira models proxy

--- agent.py:
"""Entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

An orchestrating model reads the brief and directs browsing sub-agents, one browser per website, in parallel. It
decides what to investigate where, follows up on gaps, works out the bid with exact arithmetic helpers, and finally
has a sub-agent enter and sign the bid on the submission website.
"""
import asyncio
import json
import sys
import time

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

import browsers
import run as contract
from browser import Tab
from browsing import BrowsingAgent
from calc import calculate
from llm import Model

ORCHESTRATOR = """You are the lead sales engineer preparing exactly one tender response. You cannot browse yourself:
you direct browsing assistants, one per website, and they report back. You make the decisions.

Approach:
1. Read the brief and its rules closely; they define the one correct answer. Plan which facts you need.
2. Send assistants to the websites with `investigate` — several in one turn run in parallel. Give each a precise
   task: what to find, which exact reference, which details (dates, units, status, validity, senders), and to report
   verbatim. Their first pass should survey their site for everything the rules might need; information may sit on
   any site, so ask each assistant to report anything relevant it sees.
3. Check the reports against the rules. Follow up with targeted investigations for gaps or contradictions (e.g. a
   catalogue group found in the specification must then be searched in the ERP; amendments found in Q&A must be
   applied to the right revision). Do not invent values; a fact you never saw is unknown.
4. Compute with `calculate` (exact decimal arithmetic) — never do arithmetic in your head.
5. Call `submit_bid` with the final answer JSON. It validates the JSON, then an assistant enters and signs it.
   If time is short, submit your best answer: every field scores on its own; leave optional fields out if unknown.

The clock: {minutes} minutes in total. Submit no later than ~3 minutes before the end."""


class Orchestrator:
    def __init__(self, task: dict, token: str | None, tabs: dict[str, Tab], model: Model, started: float):
        self.task, self.token, self.tabs, self.model = task, token, tabs, model
        self.credentials = {a["siteId"]: a.get("credentials", {}) for a in task["access"]}
        self.started = started
        budget = contract.seconds_left(task)
        self.deadline = time.time() + (budget if budget != float("inf") else 20 * 60)
        self.locks = {site: asyncio.Lock() for site in tabs}
        self.submitted = None

    def log(self, text: str):
        print(f"[{time.time() - self.started:6.1f}s] {text}", flush=True)

    def context(self) -> str:
        return (f"# The brief (rules apply exactly)\n{self.task['brief']}\n\n"
                f"# Answer schema\n{json.dumps(self.task['answer_schema'], ensure_ascii=False)}")

    def tools(self) -> list[dict]:
        sites = list(self.tabs)
        return [
            {"type": "function", "function": {
                "name": "investigate",
                "description": "Send a browsing assistant to one website with a precise task; returns its report.",
                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                    "site": {"type": "string", "enum": sites},
                    "task": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["site", "task"]}}},
            {"type": "function", "function": {
                "name": "calculate",
                "description": "Exact decimal arithmetic. Python-like expressions with + - * / ( ), and functions "
                               "round_half_up(x, places), ceil(x), floor(x), min, max, sum([..]). "
                               "Several named lines allowed: 'a = 2*3\\nb = a/7\\nround_half_up(b, 2)'. Returns every value.",
                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"expression": {"type": "string"}},
                               "required": ["expression"]}}},
            {"type": "function", "function": {
                "name": "submit_bid",
                "description": "Validate the final answer (JSON object per the answer schema) and have an assistant "
                               "enter and sign it on the submission website. Give any form hints you learned.",
                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                    "answer": {"type": "object"},
                    "hints": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["answer"]}}},
        ]

    async def investigate(self, site: str, task: str) -> str:
        if site not in self.tabs:
            return f"Unknown site {site}; choose one of {', '.join(self.tabs)}"
        async with self.locks[site]:
            agent = BrowsingAgent(self.model, {site: self.tabs[site]}, self.credentials, task, self.context(),
                                  name=site, deadline=self.deadline - 150, log=self.log)
            return await agent.run()

    async def submit(self, answer: dict, hints: str) -> str:
        problems = validate(answer, self.task["answer_schema"])
        if problems:
            return "The answer does not match the schema: " + "; ".join(problems)
        submission = self.task["submission"]
        if submission.get("kind") == "api":
            if not self.token:
                self.submitted = answer
                return "Local run: answer recorded, nothing is submitted."
            status, body = contract.submit_answer(self.task, self.token, answer)
            if status == 202:
                self.submitted = answer
            return f"HTTP {status}: {body[:1500]}"
        target = submission.get("siteId")
        sites = {target: self.tabs[target]}
        sites.update({s: t for s, t in self.tabs.items() if s != target})  # e.g. the mailbox for a signing code
        task = ("Enter this bid on the submission website exactly as given and submit it, following the brief's "
                "Submission section step by step (register/express interest if needed, configure every position, "
                "enter numbers in the site's number format, acknowledge documents, get the signing code where the "
                "brief says, review the summary against the answer, confirm). Use each value exactly; do not "
                "recompute. Report the receipt or any validation message verbatim.\n\nANSWER:\n"
                + json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1) + (f"\n\nHINTS:\n{hints}" if hints else ""))
        agent = BrowsingAgent(self.model, sites, self.credentials, task, self.context(), name="submit",
                              deadline=self.deadline + 120, max_steps=90, log=self.log)
        self.submitted = answer
        return await agent.run()

    async def run(self):
        minutes = round((self.deadline - time.time()) / 60)
        messages = [
            {"role": "system", "content": ORCHESTRATOR.format(minutes=minutes)},
            {"role": "user", "content": self.context() + "\n\n# Websites\n" + "\n".join(
                f"- {a['siteId']}: {a['url']}" for a in self.task["access"]) + "\n\nBegin."},
        ]
        tools = self.tools()
        while time.time() < self.deadline:
            left = self.deadline - time.time()
            if left < 300 and not self.submitted:
                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": f"Only {int(left)} s left: call submit_bid now with your best answer."})
            message = await self.model.chat(messages, tools, temperature=0.2)
            calls = message.tool_calls or []
            if message.content:
                self.log(f"[lead] {message.content[:1500]}")
            entry = {"role": "assistant", "content": message.content or ""}
            if calls:
                entry["tool_calls"] = [{"id": c.id, "type": "function",
                                        "function": {"name": c.function.name, "arguments": c.function.arguments}} for c in calls]
            messages.append(entry)
            if not calls:
                if self.submitted:
                    return
                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Continue: investigate, calculate, or submit_bid."})
                continue

            async def execute(call):
                try:
                    args = json.loads(call.function.arguments or "{}")
                except ValueError:
                    return "Error: arguments were not valid JSON"
                self.log(f"[lead] {call.function.name} {json.dumps(args, ensure_ascii=False)[:600]}")
                try:
                    if call.function.name == "investigate":
                        return await self.investigate(args["site"], args["task"])
                    if call.function.name == "calculate":
                        return calculate(args["expression"])
                    if call.function.name == "submit_bid":
                        return await self.submit(args["answer"], args.get("hints", ""))
                    return f"Unknown tool {call.function.name}"
                except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
                    return f"Error: {error}"

            results = await asyncio.gather(*(execute(c) for c in calls))
            for call, result in zip(calls, results):
                self.log(f"[lead] <- {call.function.name}: {result[:3000]}")
                messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "content": result})
            if self.submitted and any(c.function.name == "submit_bid" for c in calls):
                return


def validate(answer: dict, schema: dict) -> list[str]:
    """A small JSON-schema check for the answer's shape: required fields, types, enums, extra fields."""
    problems = []

    def check(value, rule, path):
        kind = rule.get("type")
        types = {"string": str, "number": (int, float), "integer": int, "object": dict, "array": list, "boolean": bool}
        if kind and not isinstance(value, types[kind]) or (kind in ("number", "integer") and isinstance(value, bool)):
            problems.append(f"{path}: expected {kind}")
            return
        if "enum" in rule and value not in rule["enum"]:
            problems.append(f"{path}: must be one of {rule['enum']}")
        if "const" in rule and value != rule["const"]:
            problems.append(f"{path}: must be {rule['const']!r}")
        if kind in ("number", "integer") and "minimum" in rule and value < rule["minimum"]:
            problems.append(f"{path}: below {rule['minimum']}")
        if kind == "object":
            for key in rule.get("required", []):
                if key not in value:
                    problems.append(f"{path}.{key}: required")
            props = rule.get("properties", {})
            for key, item in value.items():
                if key in props:
                    check(item, props[key], f"{path}.{key}")
                elif rule.get("additionalProperties") is False:
                    problems.append(f"{path}.{key}: not allowed")
        if kind == "array":
            for i, item in enumerate(value):
                check(item, rule.get("items", {}), f"{path}[{i}]")

    check(answer, schema, "answer")
    return problems


async def main() -> int:
    started = time.time()
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    model = Model()
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local scouting run)'}; model {model.provider}/{model.model}; "
          f"sites: {', '.join(a['siteId'] for a in task['access'])}", flush=True)
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        tabs = {}
        for index, access in enumerate(task["access"][:4]):
            available = max(len(browsers.cdp_urls()), 1)
            browser, page = await browsers.connect(playwright, index if index < available else 0)
            if index >= available:  # fewer browsers than sites: a tab of its own in the first browser
                page = await page.context.new_page()
            await page.goto(access["url"], wait_until="domcontentloaded")
            tabs[access["siteId"]] = Tab(access["siteId"], page)
        lead = Orchestrator(task, token, tabs, model, started)
        await lead.run()
    print(f"Done in {time.time() - started:.0f}s; {model.usage()}; submitted: "
          f"{json.dumps(lead.submitted, ensure_ascii=False) if lead.submitted else 'nothing'}", flush=True)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

   applied to the right revision). Do not invent values; a fact you never saw is unknown.
4. Compute with `calculate` (exact decimal arithmetic) — never do arithmetic in your head.
5. Call `submit_bid` with the final answer JSON. It validates the JSON, then an assistant enters and signs it.
   If time is short, submit your best answer: every field scores on its own; leave optional fields out if unknown.

The clock: {minutes} minutes in total. Submit no later than ~3 minutes before the end."""


class Orchestrator:
    def __init__(self, task: dict, token: str | None, tabs: dict[str, Tab], model: Model, started: float):
        self.task, self.token, self.tabs, self.model = task, token, tabs, model
        self.credentials = {a["siteId"]: a.get("credentials", {}) for a in task["access"]}
        self.started = started
        budget = contract.seconds_left(task)
        self.deadline = time.time() + (budget if budget != float("inf") else 20 * 60)
        self.locks = {site: asyncio.Lock() for site in tabs}
        self.submitted = None

    def log(self, text: str):
        print(f"[{time.time() - self.started:6.1f}s] {text}", flush=True)

    def context(self) -> str:
        return (f"# The brief (rules apply exactly)\n{self.task['brief']}\n\n"
                f"# Answer schema\n{json.dumps(self.task['answer_schema'], ensure_ascii=False)}")

    def tools(self) -> list[dict]:
        sites = list(self.tabs)
        return [
            {"type": "function", "function": {
                "name": "investigate",
                "description": "Send a browsing assistant to one website with a precise task; returns its report.",
                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                    "site": {"type": "string", "enum": sites},
                    "task": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["site", "task"]}}},
            {"type": "function", "function": {
                "name": "calculate",
                "description": "Exact decimal arithmetic. Python-like expressions with + - * / ( ), and functions "
                               "round_half_up(x, places), ceil(x), floor(x), min, max, sum([..]). "
                               "Several named lines allowed: 'a = 2*3\\nb = a/7\\nround_half_up(b, 2)'. Returns every value.",
                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"expression": {"type": "string"}},
                               "required": ["expression"]}}},
            {"type": "function", "function": {
                "name": "submit_bid",
                "description": "Validate the final answer (JSON object per the answer schema) and have an assistant "
                               "enter and sign it on the submission website. Give any form hints you learned.",
                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
                    "answer": {"type": "object"},
                    "hints": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["answer"]}}},
        ]

    async def investigate(self, site: str, task: str) -> str:
        if site not in self.tabs:
            return f"Unknown site {site}; choose one of {', '.join(self.tabs)}"
        async with self.locks[site]:
            agent = BrowsingAgent(self.model, {site: self.tabs[site]}, self.credentials, task, self.context(),
                                  name=site, deadline=self.deadline - 150, log=self.log)
            return await agent.run()

    async def submit(self, answer: dict, hints: str) -> str:
        problems = validate(answer, self.task["answer_schema"])
        if problems:
            return "The answer does not match the schema: " + "; ".join(problems)
        submission = self.task["submission"]
        if submission.get("kind") == "api":
            if not self.token:
                self.submitted = answer
                return "Local run: answer recorded, nothing is submitted."
            status, body = contract.submit_answer(self.task, self.token, answer)
            if status == 202:
                self.submitted = answer
            return f"HTTP {status}: {body[:1500]}"
        target = submission.get("siteId")
        sites = {target: self.tabs[target]}
        sites.update({s: t for s, t in self.tabs.items() if s != target})  # e.g. the mailbox for a signing code
        task = ("Enter this bid on the submission website exactly as given and submit it, following the brief's "
                "Submission section step by step (register/express interest if needed, configure every position, "
                "enter numbers in the site's number format, acknowledge documents, get the signing code where the "
                "brief says, review the summary against the answer, confirm). Use each value exactly; do not "
                "recompute. Report the receipt or any validation message verbatim.\n\nANSWER:\n"
                + json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1) + (f"\n\nHINTS:\n{hints}" if hints else ""))
        agent = BrowsingAgent(self.model, sites, self.credentials, task, self.context(), name="submit",
                              deadline=self.deadline + 120, max_steps=90, log=self.log)
        self.submitted = answer
        return await agent.run()

    async def run(self):
        minutes = round((self.deadline - time.time()) / 60)
        messages = [
            {"role": "system", "content": ORCHESTRATOR.format(minutes=minutes)},
            {"role": "user", "content": self.context() + "\n\n# Websites\n" + "\n".join(
                f"- {a['siteId']}: {a['url']}" for a in self.task["access"]) + "\n\nBegin."},
        ]
        tools = self.tools()
        while time.time() < self.deadline:
            left = self.deadline - time.time()
            if left < 300 and not self.submitted:
                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": f"Only {int(left)} s left: call submit_bid now with your best answer."})
            message = await self.model.chat(messages, tools, temperature=0.2)
            calls = message.tool_calls or []
            if message.content:
                self.log(f"[lead] {message.content[:1500]}")
            entry = {"role": "assistant", "content": message.content or ""}
            if calls:
                entry["tool_calls"] = [{"id": c.id, "type": "function",
                                        "function": {"name": c.function.name, "arguments": c.function.arguments}} for c in calls]
            messages.append(entry)
            if not calls:
                if self.submitted:
                    return
                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Continue: investigate, calculate, or submit_bid."})
                continue

            async def execute(call):
                try:
                    args = json.loads(call.function.arguments or "{}")
                except ValueError:
                    return "Error: arguments were not valid JSON"
                self.log(f"[lead] {call.function.name} {json.dumps(args, ensure_ascii=False)[:600]}")
                try:
                    if call.function.name == "investigate":
                        return await self.investigate(args["site"], args["task"])
                    if call.function.name == "calculate":
                        return calculate(args["expression"])
                    if call.function.name == "submit_bid":
                        return await self.submit(args["answer"], args.get("hints", ""))
                    return f"Unknown tool {call.function.name}"
                except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
                    return f"Error: {error}"

            results = await asyncio.gather(*(execute(c) for c in calls))
            for call, result in zip(calls, results):
                self.log(f"[lead] <- {call.function.name}: {result[:3000]}")
                messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "content": result})
            if self.submitted and any(c.function.name == "submit_bid" for c in calls):
                return


def validate(answer: dict, schema: dict) -> list[str]:
    """A small JSON-schema check for the answer's shape: required fields, types, enums, extra fields."""
    problems = []

    def check(value, rule, path):
        kind = rule.get("type")
        types = {"string": str, "number": (int, float), "integer": int, "object": dict, "array": list, "boolean": bool}
        if kind and not isinstance(value, types[kind]) or (kind in ("number", "integer") and isinstance(value, bool)):
            problems.append(f"{path}: expected {kind}")
            return
        if "enum" in rule and value not in rule["enum"]:
            problems.append(f"{path}: must be one of {rule['enum']}")
        if "const" in rule and value != rule["const"]:
            problems.append(f"{path}: must be {rule['const']!r}")
        if kind in ("number", "integer") and "minimum" in rule and value < rule["minimum"]:
            problems.append(f"{path}: below {rule['minimum']}")
        if kind == "object":
            for key in rule.get("required", []):
                if key not in value:
                    problems.append(f"{path}.{key}: required")
            props = rule.get("properties", {})
            for key, item in value.items():
                if key in props:
                    check(item, props[key], f"{path}.{key}")
                elif rule.get("additionalProperties") is False:
                    problems.append(f"{path}.{key}: not allowed")
        if kind == "array":
            for i, item in enumerate(value):
                check(item, rule.get("items", {}), f"{path}[{i}]")

    check(answer, schema, "answer")
    return problems


async def main() -> int:
    started = time.time()
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    model = Model()
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local scouting run)'}; model {model.provider}/{model.model}; "
          f"sites: {', '.join(a['siteId'] for a in task['access'])}", flush=True)
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        tabs = {}
        for index, access in enumerate(task["access"][:4]):
            available = max(len(browsers.cdp_urls()), 1)
            browser, page = await browsers.connect(playwright, index if index < available else 0)
            if index >= available:  # fewer browsers than sites: a tab of its own in the first browser
                page = await page.context.new_page()
            await page.goto(access["url"], wait_until="domcontentloaded")
            tabs[access["siteId"]] = Tab(access["siteId"], page)
        lead = Orchestrator(task, token, tabs, model, started)
        await lead.run()
    print(f"Done in {time.time() - started:.0f}s; {model.usage()}; submitted: "
          f"{json.dumps(lead.submitted, ensure_ascii=False) if lead.submitted else 'nothing'}", flush=True)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

content.text:
Julien'in push'una baktım. Özet: `agent/` klasörünü zaten uçtan uca bir ajanla doldurmuş, ama repo şu an iki ayrı geçmişe bölünmüş durumda ve birkaç riskli şey GitHub'da duruyor.

## Julien ne yapmış

GitHub'daki `main` tek bir commit (13:07, julienlmu). İçinde başlangıç kiti üzerine kurulmuş çalışan bir tasarım var:

- Bir "lider" model brief'i okuyup işi yönetiyor, her site için bir gezgin alt-ajan gönderiyor (4 tarayıcı paralel).
- Hesap için kesin ondalık bir hesap makinesi aracı, şema kontrolü ve teklifi girip imzalayan bir gönderim adımı var.
- `agent/` içinde site adresi veya giriş bilgisi aradım, çıkmadı. Bu yalnızca o tek arama; fiyat, malzeme numarası gibi değerleri ayrıca taramadım.

Benim yazmaya başladığım iskelet bununla aynı dosya yollarına denk geliyor ve aynı işi yapıyor. Durdum; taslağımı silmedim, repo dışına kenara aldım. **Önerim Julien'inkini temel almak** ve benim taslaktan yalnızca onda eksik olanı taşımak.

## Sorunlar

1. **İki geçmiş birbirine bağlı değil.** Bizim yereldeki ilk commit (Entire kurulumu, `docs/`) GitHub'a hiç gitmemiş; Julien boş repoya kendi kök commit'ini atmış. Düz `pull` çalışmıyor; iki geçmişi birleştiren bir merge commit'i gerekiyor.
2. **GitHub'da Entire yok.** Julien'in commit'inde Entire izi yok, uzakta checkpoint dalı da yok. Pazar teslimi Entire'sız repoyu reddediyor. Birleştirince kurulum dosyaları gelir, ama Julien'in kendi makinesinde `entire`'ı kurup etkinleştirmesi şart.
3. **Repo herkese açık ve keşif notları içinde.** `notes/` altında webmail, tedarikçi portalı ve ERP bulguları ile bir ham ERP dökümü var. Paketin (`agent/`) dışındalar, ama kuralımız keşif notlarının hiç commit edilmemesiydi ve diğer takımlar da okuyabiliyor.
4. **Uzaktaki `.gitignore` eksik.** `.env`, `scouting/` ve `Voice recording/` satırları yok; birleştirirken ikisini de korumam gerekir.
5. **Mimari fark.** Julien'de fiyatı model hesaplıyor (hesap makinesiyle). Bizim planımız kuralları düz kodla hesaplamaktı; para kuruşu kuruşuna karşılaştırıldığı için gezinme kısmını ondan alıp hesap motorunu yine de ayrı yazmayı öneririm.

## Senden gereken kararlar

- **Birleştirme:** İki geçmişi yerelde birleştireyim mi? Bu bir commit oluşturur (push etmem); öncesinde `entire session list` kontrolünü yaparım.
- **`notes/`:** Repodan çıkarılsın mı? Geçmişten de silmek ortak repoda geçmişi yeniden yazmak demek, o yüzden Julien'le birlikte karar verin.

Bu arada bağımlılık kurulumunu yalnızca kendi taslağım için yapmıştım; onu da kaldırdım, repoda benden kalan tek değişiklik `.gitignore`'a eklenen iki satır (`.venv/`, `__pycache__/`).

1	"""A browsing sub-agent: a model works one or more websites through numbered page views until it can report.
2	
3	The model picks every navigation target, search and document. Code only executes the action it chose, renders the
4	page as text, and keeps the conversation small: older page views are dropped once newer ones exist, while the
5	facts the model saved with `note` stay.
6	"""
7	import json
8	import time
9	
10	from browser import Tab
11	
12	TOOLS = [
13	    ("look", "Show the current page again (after waiting for it to update).", {}),
14	    ("goto", "Open a URL (absolute, or a path on the site).", {"url": "string"}),
15	    ("click", "Click the element with this number from the page view (e.g. '12' or 'f1.3' inside a frame).", {"element": "string"}),
16	    ("type", "Replace the text of an input/textarea; set enter=true to press Enter afterwards (submits searches/forms).",
17	     {"element": "string", "text": "string", "enter": "boolean"}),
18	    ("select", "Choose an option of a select element by its visible text or value.", {"element": "string", "option": "string"}),
19	    ("press", "Press a keyboard key on the page, e.g. Escape, Enter, F4, Tab.", {"key": "string"}),
20	    ("back", "Go back in the browser history.", {}),
21	    ("read_more", "Continue reading a long page view from a character offset.", {"offset": "integer"}),
22	    ("download", "Download a link target with this site's login (ZIP, CSV, PDF, document pages) and read its text.", {"url": "string"}),
23	    ("read_file", "Read a file that was downloaded earlier, from an optional offset.", {"name": "string", "offset": "integer"}),
24	    ("login", "Fill in this website's username and password on the current login form and submit it.", {}),
25	    ("note", "Save facts you read, verbatim with their exact numbers, dates, units, references and senders. Notes are "
26	     "the only thing you keep from pages you leave; your final report is built from them.", {"facts": "string"}),
27	    ("finish", "End your investigation with your report: every fact the task asked for, with where you found it, and "
28	     "what you could not find.", {"report": "string"}),
29	]
30	OPTIONAL = {"enter", "offset"}
31	
32	
33	def tool_schemas(multi_site: bool) -> list[dict]:
34	    schemas = []
35	    for name, description, params in TOOLS:
36	        properties = {key: {"type": kind} for key, kind in params.items()}
37	        required = [key for key in params if key not in OPTIONAL]
38	        if multi_site and name not in ("note", "finish"):
39	            properties["site"] = {"type": "string", "description": "which website (siteId)"}
40	            required.append("site")
41	        schemas.append({"type": "function", "function": {
42	            "name": name, "description": description,
43	            "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": properties, "required": required}}})
44	    return schemas
45	
46	
47	SYSTEM = """You are a careful sales-engineering assistant operating real business websites through a text view of the browser.
48	
49	How the page view works: each page is shown as text; elements you can use carry a number in brackets, like [12] or
50	[f1.3] (inside a frame). Act by number. Tables show as | cell | rows. "(tooltip: ...)" and "(hidden ...)" mark text
51	a person would see by hovering or expanding. Content of embedded frames (document viewers, mail bodies) follows the
52	page as "--- frame fN ---".
53	
54	Working rules:
55	- The websites are deliberately hostile: cookie walls, surveys and popups (close them; never accept surveys or
56	  unrelated offers), decoy buttons that do nothing, error pages that work on a retry, session timeouts that send you
57	  back to the login (use the login tool again), paging and "load more" controls, superseded documents shown first,
58	  look-alike records for other references. Verify that what you read belongs to the exact reference you need.
59	- Prefer direct links: if an element shows "-> /some/path", you may goto that path. For files (ZIP, CSV, PDF), use
60	  download. Use search forms with specific terms; over-broad searches may list nothing.
61	- Save every relevant fact with note as soon as you read it (verbatim numbers, units, dates, senders, record ids,
62	  status). Pages you leave are removed from your memory; notes are kept.
63	- Do not guess values. If something is missing, say so in the report.
64	- Be quick: time is limited. Several tool calls in one turn are fine when they don't depend on each other.
65	- Finish with finish(report) once you have what the task needs.
66	"""
67	
68	
69	class BrowsingAgent:
70	    def __init__(self, model, tabs: dict[str, Tab], credentials: dict[str, dict], task: str, context: str,
71	                 name: str, deadline: float, max_steps: int = 60, log=print):
72	        self.model, self.tabs, self.credentials = model, tabs, credentials
73	        self.task, self.context, self.name = task, context, name
74	        self.deadline, self.max_steps, self.log = deadline, max_steps, log
75	        self.notes: list[str] = []
76	        self.multi = len(tabs) > 1
77	
78	    def _tab(self, args: dict) -> Tab:
79	        if not self.multi:
80	            return next(iter(self.tabs.values()))
81	        site = args.get("site") or next(iter(self.tabs))
82	        if site not in self.tabs:
83	            raise ValueError(f"Unknown site {site!r}; use one of {', '.join(self.tabs)}")
84	        return self.tabs[site]
85	
86	    async def _login(self, tab: Tab) -> str:
87	        creds = self.credentials[tab.site_id]
88	        page_text = await tab.observe()
89	        frame = tab.page.main_frame
90	        password = frame.locator("input[type=password]").first
91	        if not await password.count():
92	            return "No password field on this page. " + page_text
93	        user = frame.locator("form:has(input[type=password]) input:not([type=hidden]):not([type=password]):not([type=checkbox])").first
94	        if await user.count():
95	            await user.fill(creds["username"])
96	        await password.fill(creds["password"])
97	        await password.press("Enter")
98	        await tab.settle()
99	        return await tab.observe()
100	
101	    async def _run_tool(self, name: str, args: dict) -> str:
102	        tab = self._tab(args) if name not in ("note", "finish") else None
103	        if name == "look":
104	            return await tab.observe()
105	        if name == "goto":
106	            url = args["url"]
107	            if "://" not in url:
108	                from urllib.parse import urljoin
109	                url = urljoin(tab.page.url, url)
110	            return await tab.goto(url)
111	        if name == "click":
112	            return await tab.click(str(args["element"]))
113	        if name == "type":
114	            return await tab.fill(str(args["element"]), str(args.get("text", "")), bool(args.get("enter")))
115	        if name == "select":
116	            return await tab.select(str(args["element"]), str(args["option"]))
117	        if name == "press":
118	            return await tab.press(args["key"])
119	        if name == "back":
120	            return await tab.back()
121	        if name == "read_more":
122	            return tab.read_more(int(args.get("offset") or 0))
123	        if name == "download":
124	            return await tab.fetch_file(args["url"])
125	        if name == "read_file":
126	            return tab.read_file(args["name"], int(args.get("offset") or 0))
127	        if name == "login":
128	            return await self._login(tab)
129	        if name == "note":
130	            self.notes.append(args.get("facts", ""))
131	            return "Saved."
132	        raise ValueError(f"Unknown tool {name}")
133	
134	    async def run(self) -> str:
135	        sites = "\n".join(f"- {site_id}: {tab.page.url if tab.page.url != 'about:blank' else ''} (login with the login tool)"
136	                          for site_id, tab in self.tabs.items())
137	        messages = [
138	            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM},
139	            {"role": "user", "content": f"{self.context}\n\n# Your websites\n{sites}\n\n# Your task\n{self.task}"},
140	        ]
141	        # open each site so the model starts from a real page view
142	        for tab in self.tabs.values():
143	            messages[1]["content"] += "\n\n# Current page\n" + await tab.observe()
144	        tools = tool_schemas(self.multi)
145	        for step in range(self.max_steps):
146	            remaining = self.deadline - time.time()
147	            if remaining < 20:
148	                break
149	            if remaining < 90:
150	                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Time is almost up: call finish now with what you have."})
151	            message = await self.model.chat(messages, tools, temperature=0.2)
152	            calls = message.tool_calls or []
153	            entry = {"role": "assistant", "content": message.content or ""}
154	            if calls:
155	                entry["tool_calls"] = [{"id": c.id, "type": "function",
156	                                        "function": {"name": c.function.name, "arguments": c.function.arguments}} for c in calls]
157	            messages.append(entry)
158	            if not calls:
159	                messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Use a tool: continue the task, or call finish with your report."})
160	                continue
161	            for call in calls:
162	                try:
163	                    args = json.loads(call.function.arguments or "{}")
164	                except ValueError:
165	                    args = {}
166	                if call.function.name == "finish":
167	                    report = args.get("report", "")
168	                    self.log(f"[{self.name}] finished after {step + 1} steps")
169	                    return self._report(report)
170	                self.log(f"[{self.name}] {call.function.name} {json.dumps(args, ensure_ascii=False)[:200]}")
171	                try:
172	                    result = await self._run_tool(call.function.name, args)
173	                except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001
174	                    result = f"Error: {str(error).splitlines()[0][:400]}"
175	                messages.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call.id, "content": result})
176	            self._forget_old_views(messages)
177	        self.log(f"[{self.name}] stopped without finish")
178	        return self._report("(stopped before finishing: out of steps or time)")
179	
180	    def _report(self, report: str) -> str:
181	        notes = "\n".join(f"- {n}" for n in self.notes)
182	        return f"REPORT:\n{report}\n\nNOTES TAKEN WHILE BROWSING:\n{notes or '(none)'}"
183	
184	    @staticmethod
185	    def _forget_old_views(messages: list[dict], keep: int = 2):
186	        views = [i for i, m in enumerate(messages) if m["role"] == "tool" and len(m["content"]) > 1500]
187	        for i in views[:-keep]:
188	            first = messages[i]["content"].splitlines()[0][:200]
189	            messages[i]["content"] = f"(older page view removed to save space; it began: {first})"
